label: EU(7)-PIM: benzodiazepines
title: Benzodiazepine in an older person
statement: Clonazepam | In lists: 3, 5 (A); 5 (B) | Main reason: Risk of falls, paradoxical reactions | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Start low–go slow; 0.5 mg/d. E | Alternatives: Levetiracetam[d]; gabapentin[d]; lamotrigine[d]; valproic acid[d]. E || Diazepam | In lists: 1, 4, 5 (A); 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of falling with hip fracture; prolonged reaction times; psychiatric reactions (can also be paradoxical, e.g. agitation, irritability, hallucinations, psychosis); cognitive impairment; depression | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Use the lowest possible dose, up to half of the usual dose, taper in and out, shortest possible duration of treatment. P, M Use initial oral dose of 2-2.5 mg once a day to twice a day. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; low doses of short-acting benzodiazepines such as lormetazepam (≤0.5 mg/d), brotizolam (≤0.125 mg/d); antidepressants with anxiolytic profile (SSRI[e]). E, P If used as hypnotics / sedatives: see alternatives proposed for drugs coded with N05C. || Chlordiazepoxide | In lists: 1, 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of falling with hip fracture; prolonged reaction times; psychiatric reactions (can also be paradoxical, e.g. agitation, irritability, hallucinations, psychosis); cognitive impairment; depression | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Use the lowest possible dose, up to half of the usual dose, taper in and out, shortest possible duration of treatment. P Reduce dose; for older adults use daily oral dose of 5 mg two to four times a day; in cases of severe renal failure (CrCl <10 ml/min), decrease dose by 50%. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; low doses of short-acting benzodiazepines such as lormetazepam (≤0.5 mg/d), brotizolam (≤0.125 mg/d); antidepressants with anxiolytic profile (SSRI[e]). plain_summary: Benzodiazepines raise the risk of falls, hip fracture, confusion and slowed reactions in older people, and some are listed only above a set daily dose.

medicine_groups.name: Benzodiazepines listed at any dose
medicine_groups.note: Dipotassium clorazepate is listed here as clorazepate. Ethyl loflazepate is listed as loflazepate. Several of these are not sold in Australia now, so their brand lists are empty. Tablets, capsules and injections count. Clonazepam oral drops also count. Midazolam oromucosal solution also counts.

medicine_groups.name: Benzodiazepines listed only above a daily dose
medicine_groups.note: The limits in the published list are: oxazepam above 60 mg a day, lorazepam above 1 mg a day, clotiazepam above 5 mg a day, lormetazepam above 0.5 mg a day, brotizolam above 0.125 mg a day, loprazolam above 0.5 mg a day. Only oxazepam and lorazepam are likely to be seen in Australia.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or older is supplied any Group A benzodiazepine at any dose, or a Group B benzodiazepine at a daily dose above the limit named for it. When age is missing, report only a possible finding for a Group A supply. With age unknown, report a possible Group B finding only if the dose exceeds its limit or cannot be checked. Ask whether the person is 65 or older. For Group B, also name any missing dose information. A known Group B dose at or below its limit gives no finding. For Group B, calculate the prescribed mg per day from the dose and frequency, using mg per tablet or capsule, or mg per mL for a measured volume. For as-needed directions, compare the stated or calculable maximum with the limit and describe it as the permitted maximum. For Group B at age 65 or older, if neither a daily dose nor a permitted daily maximum can be calculated, report a possible finding and ask how much the person takes in a day. Check that amount against the limit for that medicine.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was prescribed, how long it was really taken, whether it was taken as directed, and any medicine from a hospital or another pharmacy. 'When needed' directions do not show how much was actually taken.
ask_the_gp: Whether the benzodiazepine is still needed, whether the dose can be lowered or the medicine tapered and stopped, and the person's risk of falls.
